problem.title: Preventing Kafka Consumer Rebalance Storms
problem.prompt: A 24-pod Java payment-ledger consumer group reading 48 partitions at 18,000 msg/s enters a continuous rebalance loop whenever the downstream PostgreSQL ledger experiences a 90s lock spike. Each poll() fetches 500 records, pushing batch processing past max.poll.interval.ms=300000, causing LeaveGroup/rebalance storms and zero net commit progress.
requirements: Keep consumer group membership stable during 120s downstream DB latency spikes without triggering rebalances.
Preserve at-least-once offset commit semantics only after durable persistence of every record in a partition.
Eliminate stop-the-world partition revocation across unaffected pods during scaling or rolling restarts.
Bound in-memory buffered records per pod under 50 MB to prevent OOMKills during backpressure.
constraints: Downstream PostgreSQL p99 write latency can spike from 12 ms to 450 ms per batch during settlement windows.
Kafka broker cluster runs Apache Kafka 3.6 with 48 partitions per topic and 24 consumer pods.
Consumer pods have a 1 GiB JVM heap limit and 2 vCPU.

stages.learnerPrompt: Inspect the Kafka consumer metrics and logs: why are pods evicted even though the JVM is healthy and TCP heartbeats succeed?

referenceMaterial.summary: The background heartbeat thread proves TCP liveness, while max.poll.interval.ms measures application-thread progress between poll() calls.
approachSteps: Compare session.timeout.ms (45s) vs max.poll.interval.ms (300s) in broker GroupCoordinator logs.
Measure time between consecutive poll() invocations during PostgreSQL lock spikes.
tradeOffs: Raising max.poll.interval.ms hides real deadlocks for 30+ minutes.
alternatives: Use pause()/resume() to keep poll() spinning every 200 ms.
failureModes: Cascading LeaveGroup storms across all 24 pods.

stages.learnerPrompt: Propose a consumer architecture and config changes that keep poll() alive during a 120s DB stall without dropping messages or OOMing.
Review the reference implementation using bounded per-partition queues, pause()/resume(), and CooperativeStickyAssignor.

referenceMaterial.summary: Bound each partition queue to 200 records, pause() at 80% capacity, commitSync() only contiguous completed offsets, and resume() below 40%.
approachSteps: Switch partition.assignment.strategy to CooperativeStickyAssignor with static group.instance.id.
tradeOffs: Slightly higher code complexity for offset tracking vs zero rebalance storms.
alternatives: Confluent Parallel Consumer library for key-level async execution.
failureModes: Committing out-of-order offsets if worker pool processes a single partition concurrently.

stages.learnerPrompt: Why choose CooperativeStickyAssignor + static membership over simply increasing max.poll.interval.ms to 1800000?

referenceMaterial.summary: Increasing max.poll.interval.ms delays dead-pod detection to 30 minutes, whereas pause() + CooperativeStickyAssignor preserves fast failure detection and incremental rebalances.
approachSteps: Evaluate MTTR impact of 1800s max.poll.interval.ms on genuine OOM/deadlock.
Quantify partition movement: RangeAssignor moves ~100% vs CooperativeStickyAssignor moving only 2/48 partitions.
tradeOffs: Requires StatefulSet stable pod names for group.instance.id.
failureModes: Duplicate group.instance.id across two live pods causes fencing.

stages.learnerPrompt: What happens if a pod is revoked from a partition while 120 records are still sitting in its in-memory worker queue?

referenceMaterial.summary: Implement ConsumerRebalanceListener.onPartitionsRevoked to await in-flight DB writes, commit completed offsets, and drop unstarted queued records.
approachSteps: Cancel queued unstarted tasks for revoked TopicPartitions.
Await currently executing DB batch up to 10s and call commitSync() for those partitions.
tradeOffs: 10s drain adds bounded latency to graceful shutdowns.
alternatives: Abort immediately and rely on idempotent DB UPSERTs on replay.
failureModes: Failing to clear queued records causes zombie writes after another pod owns the partition.

stages.learnerPrompt: How do you prevent a single poison-pill message from permanently stalling a paused partition?

referenceMaterial.summary: Route non-retryable or 3x-failed records to a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) with original partition/offset metadata so contiguous offset commits can advance.
approachSteps: Classify exceptions into transient (SQLTransientException) vs permanent (DeserializationException, ConstraintViolation).
Publish permanent failures to <topic>.dlq and mark offset complete.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
dlqProducer.send(new ProducerRecord<>(topic + ".dlq", record.key(), record.value())).get();
markOffsetCompleted(tp, record.offset() + 1);
tradeOffs: DLQ breaks strict global ordering for that specific key.
alternatives: Per-key retry topic with exponential delay.
failureModes: DLQ producer failure must block offset commit to avoid silent drop.

spark.summary: A slow downstream dependency stalls batch processing beyond 300s, triggering GroupCoordinator eviction, stop-the-world rebalances, and duplicate redelivery across all 48 partitions.
spark.keyTakeaway: Decouple poll() liveness from slow processing via small max.poll.records, bounded worker queues with pause()/resume(), and CooperativeStickyAssignor.

problem.title: Preventing Kafka Consumer Rebalance Storms
problem.prompt: A 24-pod Java payment-ledger consumer group reading 48 partitions at 18,000 msg/s enters a continuous rebalance loop whenever the downstream PostgreSQL ledger experiences a 90s lock spike. Each poll() fetches 500 records, pushing batch processing past max.poll.interval.ms=300000, causing LeaveGroup/rebalance storms and zero net commit progress.
requirements: Keep consumer group membership stable during 120s downstream DB latency spikes without triggering rebalances.
Preserve at-least-once offset commit semantics only after durable persistence of every record in a partition.
Eliminate stop-the-world partition revocation across unaffected pods during scaling or rolling restarts.
Bound in-memory buffered records per pod under 50 MB to prevent OOMKills during backpressure.
constraints: Downstream PostgreSQL p99 write latency can spike from 12 ms to 450 ms per batch during settlement windows.
Kafka broker cluster runs Apache Kafka 3.6 with 48 partitions per topic and 24 consumer pods.
Consumer pods have a 1 GiB JVM heap limit and 2 vCPU.

concept.whyItMatters: Kafka's heartbeat thread only proves TCP liveness; max.poll.interval.ms enforces forward progress between poll() calls. When synchronous processing exceeds it, the consumer is evicted, causing cascading rebalances and duplicate processing.
whenToUse: Consumers calling external databases, HTTP APIs, or ML inference with variable tail latency.
High-throughput topics (>5,000 msg/s) where a single rebalance stalls all healthy partitions.
Kubernetes deployments with frequent HPA scale-outs or rolling updates.
whenNotToUse: Pure CPU-bound in-memory transforms completing in <50 ms per batch.
Single-partition low-volume topics (<10 msg/s) where simple synchronous poll loops suffice.
keyPoints: Heartbeat thread (session.timeout.ms=45000, heartbeat.interval.ms=3000) is independent of poll() cadence (max.poll.interval.ms=300000).
Calling consumer.pause(partitions) lets poll() continue heartbeating liveness while halting new fetches.
CooperativeStickyAssignor performs incremental two-phase rebalances, keeping unaffected partitions running.
Static group membership (group.instance.id) prevents unnecessary rebalances during brief <45s pod restarts.

tradeOffs.pro: Reduces worst-case batch duration by 10x and bounds duplicate replay window on crash.
tradeOffs.con: Increases broker fetch round-trips and reduces per-batch SQL bulk-insert amortization.

tradeOffs.factor: Async Worker Pool + pause() vs Raising max.poll.interval.ms to 1800s
tradeOffs.pro: Detects genuine deadlocks within 300s while keeping healthy partitions flowing.
tradeOffs.con: Requires explicit per-partition offset tracking to avoid committing ahead of failed workers.

failureModes.name: Premature Async Offset Commit
failureModes.description: Main poll thread commits latest polled offset while background worker fails to write to DB, causing silent data loss.
failureModes.mitigation: Disable enable.auto.commit and commit only contiguous completed per-partition offsets returned by workers.

failureModes.name: Unbounded Executor Queue OOM
failureModes.description: Poll thread keeps fetching into an unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue while DB is slow, exhausting the 1 GiB heap.
failureModes.mitigation: Use bounded queue capacity (e.g., 200 records/partition) and call consumer.pause() when queue utilization >80%.

failureModes.name: Eager Rebalance Cascade
failureModes.description: RangeAssignor revokes all 48 partitions on one pod's eviction, triggering a global 15s stop-the-world pause.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure partition.assignment.strategy=CooperativeStickyAssignor and group.instance.id per StatefulSet pod.

commonMistakes: Increasing session.timeout.ms expecting it to fix max.poll.interval.ms evictions.
Leaving enable.auto.commit=true with async worker threads.
Using RangeAssignor in multi-pod services with uneven partition counts.
Swallowing WakeupException or CommitFailedException without clearing in-flight partition buffers.

sections.content:
## Why Synchronous Poll Loops Trigger Rebalance Storms

In Kafka's consumer protocol, `ConsumerCoordinator` tracks two independent timers:
- **Session liveness** (`session.timeout.ms=45000`): maintained by a background heartbeat thread every `heartbeat.interval.ms=3000`.
- **Processing progress** (`max.poll.interval.ms=300000`): reset only when the application thread calls `KafkaConsumer.poll()`.

When `max.poll.records=500` and PostgreSQL p99 write latency spikes to `650 ms/record` during a lock contention window, a single batch takes `325s > 300s`. The coordinator sends `LeaveGroup`/eviction, revoking all 48 partitions under `RangeAssignor`. Reassigned pods re-read uncommitted offsets and hit the exact same DB lock spike, creating a self-sustaining rebalance storm with 0% throughput.

## Requirements & Constraints

- **Stability**: Zero rebalances during 120s downstream latency spikes.
- **Safety**: Strictly contiguous per-partition `commitSync()` after DB `COMMIT`.
- **Isolation**: `CooperativeStickyAssignor` + `group.instance.id` so 1 pod restart affects only 2 of 48 partitions.
- **Memory Bound**: `< 50 MB` buffered payload per pod (`1 GiB` heap ceiling).

## Capacity & Timing Math

- **Cluster throughput**: `18,000 msg/s` across `24` pods = `750 msg/s` per pod (`375 msg/s` per partition across 2 partitions/pod).
- **Payload size**: `1.5 KB` average -> `1.125 MB/s` ingress per pod.
- **Safe batch size**: `max.poll.records=50` (down from 500). At 12 ms normal batch write, `50` records take `12 ms`; at 450 ms spike, `50` records take `450 ms` (well below `300,000 ms`).
- **Queue bound**: `2,000` records/pod * `1.5 KB` = `3 MB` buffered, leaving >950 MB heap headroom.

data.title: Decoupled Poll Loop with Partition Pause/Resume

edges.label: Fetch <=50 records
edges.title: Bounded Fetch
edges.description: Poll thread fetches small batches and keeps max.poll.interval.ms timer reset every <5s.

edges.label: Enqueue per partition
edges.title: Partition Dispatch
edges.description: Records routed to per-partition ordered worker queues to preserve key ordering.

edges.label: Queue > 80% -> pause()
edges.title: Backpressure Signal
edges.description: Poll thread calls consumer.pause(tp) and poll(0) to maintain heartbeats without fetching.

edges.label: Durable batch write
edges.title: Idempotent Sink
edges.description: Workers execute SQL batch UPSERT; on completion, record highest contiguous offset.

edges.label: commitSync() + resume()
edges.title: Safe Commit & Resume
edges.description: Poll thread commits completed offsets and calls consumer.resume(tp) when queue < 40%.

data.caption: Decoupling poll() liveness from DB writes prevents GroupCoordinator eviction during 120s downstream stalls.

sections.content:
## Failure Handling

- **Revocation (`onPartitionsRevoked`)**: Drain in-flight worker tasks for revoked `TopicPartition`s up to 10s, commit their completed offsets, and discard unstarted queued records so the new owner replays cleanly.
- **Poison Pill Record**: After 3 exponential retries (`100ms, 500ms, 2s`), publish failed record + stacktrace to `<topic>.dlq` with original partition/offset headers and advance the contiguous offset.

## Final Architecture Summary

Lower `max.poll.records` from `500` to `50`, switch to `CooperativeStickyAssignor` with `group.instance.id`, disable `enable.auto.commit`, and decouple DB persistence into bounded per-partition worker queues controlled by `consumer.pause()`/`resume()`. Even during a 120s PostgreSQL lock spike, pods remain healthy in the consumer group and resume at full `18,000 msg/s` throughput immediately upon DB recovery.

options.text: Removing all timeouts and retries so requests wait indefinitely.
options.explanation: Unbounded waits exhaust worker threads and connection pools, causing total outages.
